A Photo-Crosslinkable Fluoropolymer-Passivated Flexible Neural Probe

By Howard Wang

ECE 523 · Paper 3

Kim, Koo, Kim & Jung, Biomaterials Advances 154 (2023) 213629

Overview

  1. Introduction: why build it
  2. Fabrication: how it is made

2

Goal: a soft probe that stimulates and records

Flexes with the brain

Causes less scarring than stiff silicon

Records clearly

Has low impedance, so less noise

Stimulates safely

Has a high charge injection limit, so more current without damage

APPROACH

Coat each electrode with a gold sponge + iridium oxide

A huge surface in a tiny footprint

The gold sponge (nanoporous gold). Kim et al. (2023), Fig. 3B.

3

The catch: the gold sponge needs hot acid

Silver–gold mix

Hot nitric acid

Gold sponge

The acid destroys most soft plastics

SU-8, the old insulation, failed at this step

PFPE-UA survives the acid

It is a Teflon-like plastic you can shape with light

How it is made: three steps

1

Gold wiring

Pattern gold electrodes and wires on a Teflon-like plastic base

2

Insulation with holes

Harden the blue layer with UV and wash away the spots over the electrodes

3

Acid bath

Turn each electrode into a gold sponge (circle), then add iridium oxide

Kim et al. (2023), Fig. 1. Blue = insulation (PFPE-UA), gray = plastic base (FEP), yellow = gold.

6

Adhesion and patterning in one UV exposure

Plasma activates the FEP

Ionized gas leaves reactive bonding sites

UV bonds and hardens PFPE-UA

The layer bonds to the FEP and hardens in one step

Developer opens the electrodes

A solvent washes away the unexposed resin

Patterns wash off without plasma

The plasma step creates the bond

Kim et al. (2023), Fig. 2A. Openings 10–25 µm; top on FEP, bottom on Au/FEP.

The insulation survives the acid

Kim et al. (2023), Fig. 3A–B.

The probe has 16 electrodes

Each is 20 µm wide

The insulation survives 15 min in hot acid

It shows no cracks and no peeling

SU-8 failed at this step

9

The coating makes the electrode much better

Impedance

Resistance to the signal. Lower = less noise

At 1 kHz: 510 → 29 → 4.6 kΩ

Charge storage

Total charge the surface holds (shaded)

<0.1 → 3.8 → 13.0 mC/cm²

Charge injection

Safe charge per pulse. Key for stimulation

NPG 1.05 → IrOx/NPG 5.18 mC/cm²

Kim et al. (2023), Fig. 3C–E. Black = bare Au, red = gold sponge (NPG), blue = sponge + iridium oxide (IrOx/NPG).

10

Charge injection limit vs. other materials

NPG (this work)

1.05

Activated / sputtered IrOx

1–5

Electrodeposited PtIr

3.85

Titanium nitride

4.45

Porous Pt nanorods

4.45

IrOx/NPG (this work)

5.18

Polymer + CNT composites

> 7

Among the highest charge injection limits of FDA-approved implant materials.

CIL in mC/cm², as cited by Kim et al. (2023), refs 10, 11, 32–38.

FOUR CHECKS

1 Can it listen?

2 Can it trigger a response?

3 Do the neurons react normally?

4 Does the effect last an hour?

Figure: Azimzadeh et al., MethodsX 12:102544 (2024), CC BY 4.0; labels added. Kim et al. setup: Section 5.5.

12

Check 1: it hears single neurons

A Cortex: spikes 3–6× above the noise

B Sorting: two different neurons

C Hippocampus: one neuron, clearly

Result: clean recordings of single neurons

Kim et al. (2023), Fig. 4. Each spike is one neuron firing.

13

Check 2: a tiny pulse triggers a response

Response: grows with the pulse

The dip is the neurons answering

Charge: only ~3 nC per pulse

Typical studies use 10–1000 nC

Result: a clear response from very little charge

Kim et al. (2023), Fig. 5B. Pulse strengths: 20, 80 and 150 µA.

14

Check 3: the neurons react normally

D Gap between pulses: 50 ms

The second response is stronger

E Biggest boost: ~30%

It matches textbook results

Result: the neurons around the probe behave normally

Kim et al. (2023), Fig. 5D–E. Each line is one recording electrode.

15

Check 4: the response stays boosted for an hour

Before the burst: steady

At the arrow: a strong burst

After 60 min: still 20–40% higher

Result: LTP, the lab model of memory

Kim et al. (2023), Fig. 6B. Each dot is the response size at one moment.

17

Limitations and open questions

AUTHORS ACKNOWLEDGE

Thick probe (~100 × 200 µm)

It causes more damage on insertion

Short tests only

No test lasted longer than a day

Small, variable LTP

Electrode placement is the likely cause

MY QUESTIONS

Unmeasured adhesion

It was only shown to survive processing

Small sample, no control

Only 3 rats were used, with no control electrode

Inconsistent methods

Burst protocol, gold thickness and I/O settings differ

18

Takeaways

1 A new insulation survives hot acid

A gold-sponge coating can now go on a soft probe

2 The coating makes electrodes much better

Impedance drops ~110× and safe charge rises ~5×

3 One soft probe stimulates and records

It needs very little charge and induces LTP lasting over an hour
